model_definitions_in_authors_terms.xFP: expected fantasy points — 'the half-PPR points an average player would score with the same opportunities'. Per-opportunity model on field position, down/distance, time/score, formation, air yards + direction (targets), run direction (carries). DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES QB quality, offensive line, team strength, betting lines, and weather — it prices the opportunity, not the context. Trained on 2009-2025 and then FROZEN (the model does not refit in-season). AUTHOR'S STATED LIMIT: xFP holds up better season-to-season than raw points but 'is not a better forecast of future points than the points themselves' — recorded verbatim because a source that publishes its own ceiling is read differently from one that does not. NOTE: this xFP is Box Score Scout's own model; the PFF xFP at C-305 is a different model under the same label
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.kicker_model: logistic regression per kick type on distance, season, indoors/outdoors, wind, cold, and altitude; rolling refit on the current season + prior 4 seasons. Outputs: make-prob per kick, xFG% (expected FG percentage), FGOE% (field goals over expected), KPA (kicking points added)
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.player_comps: ~12 role/efficiency stats per position, compared against the same-season position cohort (players with >=50% of team games); in-season profiles BLEND current games + the prior 2 seasons + the position average + draft round (years 1-2). Calibration as published: two random seasons score ~60% similarity; the closest comps land in the 80s-90s
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.team_comps: 10 percentiles per team season (offensive + defensive EPA/play, 4 success rates, 2 explosive rates, PROE, plays/game); comps are nearest by distance across those percentiles
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.athletic_score: combine/pro-day drills ranked WITHIN position, weighted by how much each drill predicted draft position, then ranked across positions
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.excitement: game excitement index = the sum of |win-probability change| across every play; 1.00 = one full swing
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.play_callers_db: every offensive and defensive play caller since 1999, ranked on their unit's EPA/play, success %, etc. (data: @SamHoppen's play-caller file). CROSS-REFERENCE: this is an external, public instance of the coaching-transition premise family — SPEC-C P-014 analogue (play-caller changes as premises); a play-caller change is a stamped, checkable event and this DB is where the before/after unit numbers live in public
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.percentile_convention: percentiles rank against ALL qualified seasons since 1999, NOT within-season; defensive-allowed percentiles are flipped (a high percentile = allowed little)
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.data_coverage: tables from 1999; xFP from 2009; PROE from 2006; NGS from 2016 (source credit as the site states it)
model_definitions_in_authors_terms.features: player/team stats + pages, statistical comps, a charts tool with PNG export, Fantasy Board (fantasy-points-over-replacement big board), Game Finder + Season Finder
